cells.note: Orphaned/free left-side cards route to OmniUnanchoredBin correctly (anchor-state-classify-contract.test.ts; OmniViewPanel.tsx:405-435), but OrphanedFootnoteCard omits data-card-key so its halo never paints across surfaces; fold-collapsed-section cards are silently dropped from omni with no recovery bin.

Stale-anchor recovery for left subjects is mostly N-A at the omni layer (footnote/citation atoms re-anchor by moving the marker; reports clear dead anchorId via virgil-anchor-orphaned listener at useReports.ts:407-416). Citation id regeneration on re-parse (useCitations.ts:357-374; comment EditorPane.tsx:1170-1182) means a code-view round-trip re-parse can invalidate the omni-held selectedCitationId + pin (keyed by id). Whether an in-session re-parse actually fires (vs only on doc load) needs a live code-view↔TipTap sync to confirm the selection/pin drift.

Footnote/citation/example are 1-atom-per-card (no true dup-on-same-anchor). Multi-paragraph reports DO produce N omni rows (@0/@1, Reports/omni.tsx:83-95) sharing one card.id; selecting any row sets selectedReportCardId=card.id so ALL rows halo (intended), but marker/gutter-click pin alignment can't disambiguate or even match the @i wrapper.

Float/popout + morph remap is handled (convertCardWithRemap, EditorPane.tsx:863-918). But single-selection is NOT enforced across the report/cutter/revision omni setters (omni-host.tsx:357-365 cross-clear nothing) leaving multiple halos; multi-anchor report marker clicks can't align/pin (no @suffix in omniKey); morph leaves an orphaned pin; orphaned footnote lacks data-card-key for cross-surface paint; citation copy-citekey clipboard is unguarded.

Strip chrome (toggle/collapse via collapseLeft/expandLeft, split via toggleSplit, hide-all via toggleOmniHideAllCards, reorder via movePanel) wired in IconStrip (EditorPane.tsx:4839-4913). No count badge is rendered on the omni strip itself (omni has no per-strip count badge — that's a docked-panel concern, N-A here). Toggle/collapse/split/hide-all paths each mutate prefs cleanly.

Filter menu toggle/Default-view/category-resolution (categoryOf) work; outside-focus + unanchored bins classify correctly. But movePanel doesn't update omniCategories so a moved panel's cards get stuck on the old strip with no filter UI to remove them; the outside-focus bin's hardcoded topPx:30 overlaps the EXPANDED unanchored bin; fold-collapsed cards vanish with no bin.

findings.subject: omni-left
findings.symptom: After dragging a left-side panel (e.g. Reports) to the right strip, its cards keep showing in the LEFT omni column and the user has NO way to turn them off — the left filter menu no longer lists that category, yet the cards persist on the left.
findings.suspectedRootCause: movePanel rewrites prefs.placements only; it never touches prefs.omniCategories. categorySides re-derives from placements (so the panel's filter ROW jumps to the destination strip's menu — localCats = OMNI_CATEGORIES.filter(c => categorySides[c] === side)), but visibleItems gates purely on enabledCategories.has(cat) (the raw per-side omniCategories set), which still contains the moved category for the source side. The displayed-set filter and the menu-visibility filter use two different keys (enabledCategories vs categorySides), so they desync the instant a panel moves between strips.

evidence.note: movePanel updates placements/activeLeft/activeRight only — no omniCategories mutation in the returned patch (lines 1030-1035).
localCats (the rows the filter menu shows) = OMNI_CATEGORIES.filter(c => categorySides[c] === side) — derived from placements, so a moved category's row leaves this side's menu.

visibleItems filters ONLY on enabledCategories.has(cat) (the raw omniCategories[side] set), with no categorySides cross-check — so a category enabled on this side still renders even after its panel moved away.
getOmniEnabled(side) returns new Set(omniCategories[side]) — never reconciled against placements.

reproSteps: Open the left omni column with Reports cards visible (Reports enabled in omniCategories.left).
Drag the Reports panel from the left strip to the right strip (movePanel('reports','right')).
Observe: Reports cards still cascade in the LEFT omni column.
Open the LEFT filter menu — Reports is no longer listed (localCats dropped it because categorySides.reports is now 'right'), so there is no toggle to hide it on the left.
findings.suspectedClass: Any pref derived from two independent sources that should move in lockstep (placements vs omniCategories). Same class as: a category enabled on a side whose panel was closed; deriveCategorySides falling back to registry omniSide while omniCategories keeps a user override. The fix is to either gate visibleItems on categorySides too, or have movePanel migrate the category's enabled-membership to the destination side.

findings.subject: omni-left
findings.symptom: When focus view is active AND there are unanchored cards, expanding the 'N unanchored' bin covers the '◎ N outside focus' pill, making it unclickable and visually overlapping the unanchored card list.
findings.suspectedRootCause: Both bins are position:absolute siblings inside the same cascade pod. The outside-focus bin is hardcoded to top:30px (topPx={...>0 ? 30 : 0}) — a number measured ONLY against the COLLAPSED unanchored pill height (~26.5px, per the inline comment). When the unanchored bin is EXPANDED its body grows downward well past 30px, but the outside-focus bin stays pinned at 30px. The unanchored bin's z-20 sits above the outside-focus bin's z-19, so the expanded unanchored list paints over and intercepts clicks on the outside-focus pill.

evidence.note: topPx={free.length + orphaned.length > 0 ? 30 : 0} — magic 30px assumes the unanchored bin is exactly the collapsed pill height.
Unanchored bin: position:absolute, top:4, zIndex:20.
When expanded the unanchored bin renders its list inline (mt-1 ... overflow-y-auto), growing downward from top:4 — height far exceeds 30px.
Outside-focus bin: position:absolute, top:topPx(=30), zIndex:19 — drawn UNDER the expanded unanchored list.

reproSteps: Activate focus view with at least one card anchored outside the focus band (populates the outside-focus bin).
Have at least one unanchored/orphaned card so the 'N unanchored' bin is present.
Click the 'N unanchored' pill to expand it.
Observe the expanded unanchored list overlaps and covers the '◎ N outside focus' pill below it; the outside-focus pill can no longer be clicked.
findings.suspectedClass: Hardcoded layout offsets between independently-sized absolute siblings (lead #10). Same class: any future third bin stacked below these; the unanchored pill's own height changing if the count reaches 3+ digits or the orphan badge grows. The robust fix is flow-stacking the bins or measuring the predecessor's live height.

findings.subject: omni-left
findings.symptom: Two omni cards can show a selection halo at once — e.g. select a footnote (marker or omni card), then click a Report omni card; the footnote stays haloed alongside the report. Single-selection is not enforced in the omni column.
findings.suspectedRootCause: Every left card paints its halo from `isHaloed = ac.selected || isSelected`, where ac.selected reads the single-slot cardStore and isSelected reads the per-side selected*Id context. The per-side setters are inconsistent: setFootnoteInOmni/setCitationInOmni/setExampleInOmni cross-clear a SUBSET (citation/note/archive/todo) but the report/cutter/revision setters (setReportInOmni/setCutterInOmni/setRevisionInOmni) clear NOTHING. So selecting a report leaves selectedFootnoteId set; cardStore moves to the report (clearing ac.selected for the footnote) but the footnote's per-side isSelected fallback keeps it haloed. The two selection axes (cardStore single-slot vs the bag of per-side ids) are never reconciled.

evidence.note: setRevisionInOmni / setCutterInOmni / setReportInOmni each call ONLY their own setter — no cross-clear of footnote/citation/note/etc.
setFootnoteInOmni clears citation/note/archive/todo but NOT example/report/cutter/revision/error — partial, asymmetric cross-clear.
isHaloed = ac.selected || isSelected — the per-side isSelected (selectedFootnoteId) keeps the halo even after cardStore moves to another card.
onClick runs ac.onActivate() (cardStore.select report) + onSelect(report.id) (setReportInOmni) — neither path clears the stale footnote/citation per-side id.

reproSteps: Click a footnote in-text marker (or its omni card) → footnote omni card haloed; selectedFootnoteId set.
Click a Report omni card in the same left column.
Observe both the footnote card AND the report card display the selection halo simultaneously.
findings.suspectedClass: Dual selection sources (`ac.selected || isSelected`) with a per-kind id bag that lacks a single mutual-exclusion chokepoint. Every left/right omni card kind whose per-side setter doesn't fully cross-clear is a sibling. Right-column kinds (notes/todo/archive/cutter/revision) share the same `|| isSelected` pattern and the same incomplete cross-clear, so the same double-halo is reachable there too.

findings.subject: omni-left
findings.symptom: Clicking the in-text gutter marker of a Report anchored to MULTIPLE paragraphs selects/opens the card but never pin-aligns it to the click — the card jumps to its natural cascade Y instead of staying at the marker's vertical position.
findings.suspectedRootCause: A multi-paragraph report emits N omni rows whose ids carry an `@<index>` suffix (Reports/omni.tsx builds `${baseId}@${pi}`), and each wrapper stamps data-omni-entry-wrapper with that suffixed id. But the marker/gutter click path computes omniKey = cardPopKey('report', id) (NO suffix), and alignOmniCardWithClick / the virgil-card-jumped handler look up `[data-omni-entry-wrapper="${cardId}"]` with the unsuffixed key — which matches none of the @0/@1 wrappers. The retry rAF also fails (the key never gains a suffix), so requestPin is never called. The marker-click detail carries only entityId=card.id with no anchor index, so even with two gutter markers the handler can't pick the right @i row.

evidence.note: omniId = `${baseId}${suffix}` where suffix = pids.length > 1 ? `@${pi}` : '' — multi-anchor rows get @0/@1; wrapper id = this suffixed id.
routeAnchorClick: omniKey = cardPopKey(route.cardKind, id) — unsuffixed; passed to alignOmniCardWithClick (line 157).
alignOmniCardWithClick queries document.querySelector(`[data-omni-entry-wrapper="${cardId}"]`) — no match for a multi-anchor report's @i wrapper, so pinTop is never published.
virgil-card-jumped handler has the same unsuffixed-key lookup — same miss for jumpToCard on a multi-anchor report.

reproSteps: Create a Report linked to two paragraphs (two paragraph anchors → omni rows ...@0 and ...@1).
Click the report's gutter marker on either anchored paragraph.
Observe the report card is selected/opened but does not pin to the click Y — alignOmniCardWithClick finds no wrapper for the unsuffixed key and silently no-ops.
findings.suspectedClass: Any omni item whose wrapper id diverges from the card's canonical cardPopKey — the multi-anchor `@i` suffix is the only current divergence, but the same break would hit any future per-anchor row fan-out. The fix is to align on a wrapper id the marker path can reconstruct (or have the marker event carry the anchor index).

findings.subject: omni-left
findings.symptom: An orphaned footnote card selected/hovered in one surface does not show its selection/hover halo in another surface (e.g. a popped-out float of the same orphan, or a docked Footnotes panel instance).
findings.suspectedRootCause: OrphanedFootnoteCard never sets data-card-key (it passes neither a cardKey prop to EditableCard nor data-card-key in extraDataAttrs — only the omni builder's data-omni-entry). The cross-surface halo reconciler paints panel cards by sweeping `[data-card-key="..."]`; with no such attribute the orphan can only be painted by its local `isHaloed` boolean within the bin. The anchored FootnoteCard, by contrast, stamps data-card-key in extraDataAttrs (line 145) and passes cardKey (line 151).

evidence.note: OrphanedFootnoteCard renders EditableCard with extraDataAttrs={extraDataAttrs} and NO data-card-key / no cardKey prop.
Anchored FootnoteCard DOES inject `"data-card-key": cardKey` — the orphan path dropped it.
Panel-card sweep keys entirely on [data-card-key]; a card without it is never painted across surfaces.

reproSteps: Create an orphaned footnote (a \footnote{} whose callout was deleted) so it appears in the omni unanchored bin.
Pop the orphan out to a float (or open a second Footnotes surface).
Select/hover the orphan in one surface and observe the other surface's copy does not gain the halo/hover paint.
findings.suspectedClass: Any card variant that forgets to stamp data-card-key (the cross-surface paint key). Orphan/fallback render paths are the usual offenders since they diverge from the primary card body. Worth auditing other orphan/empty-state card variants for the same omission.

findings.subject: omni-left
findings.symptom: Folding a section silently removes its anchored omni cards from the column with no 'N folded' bin or count — unlike focus view, which collects out-of-band cards into a recoverable 'N outside focus' bin. The user gets no in-omni signal that cards exist behind the fold.
findings.suspectedRootCause: The fold filter (pass 1 in displayedItems) DROPS any item whose resolved block index is in hiddenTopLevel, rather than stamping it for a bin the way the focus filter (pass 2) stamps outsideFocus. The design comment explicitly chooses to drop ('drop — card lives in a collapsed section'), reasoning the docked panel still lists them; but at the omni layer this is an asymmetric, signal-less hide.

evidence.note: Pass 1 fold filter: if hiddenTopLevel.has(bi) the item is NOT pushed (dropped) — no bin, no count.
Pass 2 focus filter STAMPS outsideFocus instead of dropping, expressly to avoid 'silent data loss' — the fold path does not get the same treatment.

reproSteps: Anchor a card (note/report) inside a section.
Fold that section (heading chevron).
Observe the card disappears from the omni column with no 'folded' bin or count — only unfolding brings it back.
findings.suspectedClass: Asymmetric handling of two 'anchor hidden in-text' conditions (fold vs focus). The same rationale that justified the outside-focus bin (don't silently hide user cards) argues a folded-section bin or count. Low because it's fully recoverable and the docked list is unaffected.

findings.subject: omni-left
findings.symptom: After morphing a popped/pinned Report to a Report-Request (or back), a stale omni pin can linger keyed to the old kind until a different card is clicked.
findings.suspectedRootCause: The omni pin store keys requests by the omni item id = cardPopKey(kind,id), which bakes the kind. convertCardWithRemap remaps the FLOAT popout key (remapCardPopKey) but nothing remaps an active omniPinStore entry. After report→report-request the new omni row id is float:card:report-request:<id> while any active pin still references float:card:report:<id>; OmniViewPanel matches pins by cardId, so the pin no longer matches the (new-kind) wrapper and is never applied nor cleared — it just sits until requestPin replaces it on the next interaction.

evidence.note: clearPin only fires explicitly; no kind-change remap. Pins persist until a replacing requestPin.
convertCardWithRemap calls viewPrefs.remapCardPopKey(old,new) for the FLOAT key but does not remap the omniPinStore entry.
isPinned = pinRequest?.cardId === item.id — a kind-suffixed id mismatch silently drops the pin (no overlap, no error).

reproSteps: Click a Report omni card so it pins (pin keyed float:card:report:<id>).
Morph it to a Report-Request via the kind chevron.
Observe the omni row re-renders under float:card:report-request:<id>; the prior pin no longer matches and lingers stale in the store.
findings.suspectedClass: Any module that keys interaction state by a kind-baked float key but isn't included in the morph remap (convertCardWithRemap remaps poppedOutCards + cardFloatPositions but not omniPinStore, nor the per-side selected*Id which is keyed by raw id and survives). Low impact: the pin is one-shot and self-replaces on the next click.

findings.subject: omni-left
findings.symptom: A citation the user deliberately created unanchored (panel-only, never placed in text) shows in the omni unanchored bin with the red 'No anchor in document' orphan badge, reading as an error/orphan rather than an intentional unanchored entry.
findings.suspectedRootCause: buildCitationOmniItems classifies anchorState purely on pos: pos==null ⇒ 'orphaned', never 'free'. There is no flag distinguishing 'marker missing (truly orphaned)' from 'panel-created, intentionally unanchored'. The bin then routes every orphaned item under a BadgeOrphaned (error theme). The contract test explicitly documents this as current behavior, so it's a known classification merge, not an accident — but it conflates two user-meaningful states.

evidence.note: anchorState: pos == null ? 'orphaned' : 'anchored' — no 'free' branch for citations, even panel-created unanchored ones.
Test comment: 'this includes panel-created unanchored citations: current behavior classifies them orphaned too.'
Orphaned rows render with BadgeOrphaned (error theme) — applied to intentionally-unanchored citations as well.

reproSteps: Create a citation via the panel without placing a \cite in the document (panel-only unanchored citation).
Open the omni unanchored bin.
Observe the citation carries the red 'No anchor in document' orphan badge as if its marker were lost.
findings.suspectedClass: Conflating 'free' (never anchored, intentional) with 'orphaned' (anchor lost) at the pos==null fork. The footnote builder distinguishes them (separate orphanedFootnotes list ⇒ 'orphaned' vs would-be 'free'), but citations and examples collapse both into 'orphaned'. Cosmetic/UX, recoverable.

findings.subject: omni-left
findings.symptom: Clicking 'copy citekey' on a citation card (rendered in the omni column) throws / produces an unhandled promise rejection in an insecure or clipboard-unavailable context, with no user feedback.
findings.suspectedRootCause: copyCitekey calls navigator.clipboard.writeText(...).then(...) with no guard for navigator.clipboard being undefined and no .catch on the promise. In a non-secure context (or a sandboxed iframe without clipboard-write permission) navigator.clipboard is undefined → synchronous TypeError in the click handler; where it exists but rejects, the missing .catch surfaces as an unhandled rejection. The 'copied' confirmation only runs on resolve, so failures are silent to the user.

evidence.note: void navigator.clipboard.writeText(trimmed).then(...) — no `navigator.clipboard?` guard, no .catch fallback.
Sibling unguarded navigator.clipboard usage — same defect class elsewhere in the card spine.

reproSteps: Load Virgil in a context where navigator.clipboard is unavailable (insecure origin / restricted iframe).
Open a citation card in the omni column and click the copy-citekey control.
Observe a thrown TypeError / unhandled rejection and no copied feedback.
findings.suspectedClass: Unguarded navigator.clipboard across the codebase (lead #12). At least suggestion-fields.tsx shares it; any copy-to-clipboard affordance lacking the `if (!navigator.clipboard) return` guard + .catch is a sibling. Low because Virgil normally runs on https/localhost where clipboard is present.
